{
  "explanation": "The central tree retains the boundary's major components and contracts while reducing the seed from 147 to 102 lines (30.6%) and from 10,965 to 7,505 characters (31.6%). Six peripheral trees expand composition, MCP scope, HTTP admission, chat streaming, live sockets and evaluation. [M] denotes modular structure, [C] calls, [O] ownership and [D] data dependency; these perspectives can coexist within each tree. Edges attach to the corresponding central concept lines. Positions leave gaps between the measured text bounds.

Only context.json and seed.json supply evidence. Composition details come from bootstrap.ts; MCP details from infrastructure/mapping/mcp/server.ts and scripts/mapping/mcp.ts; admission from vitePlugin.ts, apiAccess.ts, http.ts and agentRoutes.ts; streaming from agentChatRoutes.ts and liveCanvasRoutes.ts; evaluation from evalRoutes.ts and the mapping router.

Corrections and qualifications: the seed's broad public-session/event filtering claim is narrowed to the explicit publicSession/publicEvent paths; list and generations routes delegate directly, so their filtering cannot be inferred here. The socket implementation permits errors before successful attach/publish, rather than enforcing that the first validated frame selects a role. Fake mode switches selected runtimes, while Agent Chat still receives StdioCodexConnection and diff workflows receive PiDiffSessionRuntime. Diagram-tool validation without a chat binding also applies to target-bound connections, so 'unbound' was too ambiguous.

New source-grounded details include context-source resolution, the distinction between MCP readOnlyHint and HTTP gate exemptions, extra MCP callbacks omitting the binding header, precise snapshot shortening, weak/wildcard ETag matching, and evaluation input dependencies. Imported service implementations and schemas are not supplied; delegation does not establish their internal validation, persistence or authorization behavior.",
